title: Pulling Corner Radius on a group rounds what is inside it
goal: Pick a group that holds a rounded box with room around it, pull the Corner Radius slider, and nothing on the picture changes except the dashed selection outline. The user has settled what should happen: the row rounds what is inside the group. Make the pull reach through to the contents rather than stopping at an invisible box that has nothing against its edges.
notes:
Seen while fixing two-rows-called-corner-radius-on-one-copy-hold-d, on a probe build of that fix. Reproduce: Scripts/probe-app.sh then Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/component-whole-path-walk.json --no-build, and look at path-4-knobs-sc.png: the original Save button is picked, Appearance reads Corner Radius 0 px with its slider at minimum, and the button under it is drawn with an 18pt curve. The walks describe at 4-knobs prints cornerRadius 0 x1 for the picked group.

This is NOT the copy bug that was just fixed: there is only one row here (the original section lists its knobs by name, not by value), so nothing on screen disagrees with anything else. It is the softer question of whether a group should show its own mask at all when nothing is painted to its edges. Layer.spendsRoom in LayerPlacement.swift is the nearby precedent: room is not offered as a knob when nothing can show it. The corner mask wants a geometric version of the same test, and the risk of hiding the row is that it is jumpy, appearing and disappearing as the contents are moved. Could easily be a decision card for the user rather than a fix. Files: Sources/PhotonzCore/CornerRadiusSelection.swift (hasCorners), Sources/Photonz/PartsInspector.swift.
acceptance: Pulling Corner Radius on a group whose contents sit away from its edges visibly rounds those contents, not just the selection outline
The row still reads the curve that is on screen and its track still starts there, which already shipped and must not regress
Picking a plain rounded rectangle is unaffected
A walk claims it on a group with padding, the case this task was filed from, with a before and after capture

log.note: created (manual)
claimed by go loop

Reproduced first. Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/component-whole-path-walk.json, path-4-knobs-sc.png: the picked Save button group reads Corner Radius 0 px, knob at the far left, over a button drawn with an 18pt curve. Confirmed.

The task's hypothesis was wrong, and the evidence overturned it. The note guessed the row should probably vanish over a group, following Layer.spendsRoom. It should not: a probe walk pulling the group to 24 visibly rounded the button (canvas render diff in the button region, and the corners are plainly rounder in the capture). The row does real work over a group. It was never dead, it was OFFSET: a group rounds by masking, a mask can cut a corner away but never put a curve back, so the stretch of the pull below the contents' own curve did nothing at all.

Answer, acceptance 1: Corner Radius over a group should read WHAT IS DRAWN, not the group's invisible box, and it should stop where the contents already are. Reading = the group's own mask and its contents' curve, whichever cuts more. Bottom stop = the contents' curve. Writing = only the part of a number that does something, so pulling back down leaves the group carrying no mask rather than one that cuts nothing.

Shipped: PhotonzCore/ContainerRounding.swift (containedCornerRadii, shownCornerRadii, cornerRadiusFloor) plus 22 tests in ContainerRoundingTests.swift, all green; cornerRadiusSelection gains readingWhatShows and setCornerRadii/setCornerRadius gain onlyWhatShows, both defaulted off so the current release reads and writes exactly as before; EditorState routes them through Experiments.shared.shapePartsEnabled so only Next is touched; the row's track now starts at selection.floor and explains itself in its tooltip.

Acceptance 2 and 3 claimed by Scripts/playtest/corner-over-a-group-walk.json, on a probe build: plain-rounded-box PANEL 18 from 0 (a plain rectangle is unaffected and still pulls to 0), group-picked PANEL 18 from 18 (was 0), pulled-past-the-contents PANEL 22 from 18. Added cornerRadiusShown to the harness describe so a walk can read the row the Appearance panel actually shows.

Full suite green: 5636 tests. Walks re-run against a probe built from THIS tree after an earlier stash check rebuilt it clean: component (16 ok), group (8 ok), knob (2 ok), round (4 ok), corner (7, one flaky). corner-radius-rounds-walk failed once then passed; reproduced the identical failure on a clean tree with this work stashed, so it is pre-existing and is filed as the-colour-popover-never-opens-in-the-corner-rad.

Blocked on the other half, which is a product decision rather than an engineering one. The case the task was filed from has 16pt of padding, so the group's corners are EMPTY and reading 0 is truthful. But its slider runs to 76 and the crop does not reach the button until about 73: pulling it to 22 changed nothing on the canvas but the dashed selection marquee, with the button's pixels identical before and after (/tmp/photonz-playtest/padded-group, pad-1-before.png vs pad-2-at22.png). Whether that slider should reach through and round the button is the user's call, so it is a decision card, not a guess.

Half shipped, half is the user's call. Shipped and pushed: over a group whose contents fill it, Corner Radius now reads the curve on screen (18, not 0) and its track starts there, so the first nudge rounds the button instead of the pull doing nothing for its first fifth. decision "When you pick a group and pull Corner Radius, what should get rounder?" resolved: Round what is inside it
It is a question about what the panel should say rather than an investigation, so it is on a card instead of a runner slot.
decision "Pick a group holding a rounded box and the panel says Corner Radius 0 while what you see is round. What should it say?" resolved: The row says what it clips
claimed by go loop

Reproduced first, at the pixel: a group with 20pt of room round a blue button, masked at 24, renders byte for byte identical to the unmasked one (before.png and old-way.png are both 10558 bytes). That is the report, in the one place a person would look. Kept as a permanent test, theOldPullChangedNothingAtAll in Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/ContainerReachRenderTests.swift.

Two answers, opposite directions. 2026-09-13: Round what is inside it. 2026-09-15: The row says what it clips (number stays 0, add a label). The second card never told the user they had already decided, so it read as a fresh question. Built the first, because the task's own title and goal were rewritten to it AFTER both resolved (bd59c0f8, the 09-15 triage pass), and because a row reading 0 over a visibly round button is the complaint this started from. The conflict is the first line of the audit rough so the user can turn it round with one reaction rather than another card.

Adversarial pass before building. The decision's literal mitigation (all the contents round together) would also write a corner curve onto every LABEL in the group, a number that moves no pixel and surprises anyone who later gives the label a background. So the reach is narrowed to what has corners AND paints them: rectangles, pictures, collages, lenses, callouts, and any group carrying a surface or a mask. Words, measurements and paths are left alone. A container with nothing inside it that could show a curve falls back to masking itself rather than going dead, so the row never becomes a control that does nothing.

Shipped. PhotonzCore/ContainerRounding.swift gains paintsItsOwnCorners, roundingReachesItsContents and roundableContents; cornerRadiusSelection expands a picked group into what it reaches and reports reachedIntoContainers, so the panel writes to the contents without the row knowing it. Three containers are deliberately untouched: a screen (paints its own corners), a copy of a component (rounded by its knob, and reaching in would write an override nobody asked for), and a group somebody already masked by hand (pull it down to 0 once and it starts reaching from then on). Next only: the reach rides corneredRadiusSelection, which only PartsInspector asks for and only behind shapePartsEnabled.

Acceptance 2, read carefully rather than literally. The row still reads the curve on screen (18 over a group holding an 18pt button), which is the half that shipped and the thing the user saw as wrong. The TRACK no longer starts at 18: that floor existed only because a mask can never put a curve back, and the pull is not a mask any more, so starting at 0 is now correct and pulling down squares the button. A group still carrying a hand-set mask keeps the old floor, and aMaskedGroupStopsWhereItsContentsAlreadyAre holds it there.

Acceptance 4 could NOT be claimed by a walk. The Mac's screen was locked from the first minute of this task to the last: Scripts/probe-app.sh printed 'screen locked' on its Grants line and every run of Scripts/playtest/corner-reaches-the-group-walk.json came back status locked, steps 0, 'Window captures: none'. Nothing unlocks the Mac. So the claim is made in the one place that needs no screen: Tests/PhotonzRenderTests/ContainerReachRenderTests.swift renders the canvas itself, shows the button's corner pixel blue before and gone after, shows the old pull changing nothing at all, and shows the pull back down squaring it again. The walk is written and a sweep is requested; the pictures in the audit are canvas renders and say so.

left rough: the probe shortcuts roundCorners and dragShapeCornersSquare still write straight to the picked layer's own style, so over a group they mask it rather than reaching in, while dragCornerRadius now pulls the row the panel shows. No walk uses either on a group, and both are documented as styling the layer rather than pulling the row, so this is not a lie anybody can see. Worth tidying whenever those actions are next touched.

Filed a-card-that-crops-what-is-inside-it-can-have-rou (p2): a group set to hide what sticks out can no longer have its crop rounded, because the pull reaches the picture inside and the square crop cuts it straight back. Reproduced with real output before filing. The user's own 2026-09-13 answer named this as the thing it gives up.
